newsitem.title: THAILAND: FOCUS - Two-tier baht market to hurt Thailand image.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Two-tier baht market to hurt Thailand image.

text.p: Flushed with success in crushing baht speculators, Thailand is expected to maintain its policy of blocking funds used for profiting from the currency, at least for a while.
However, the Bank of Thailand's determination to restore baht stability in this way risks tarnishing Thailand's long-term image as a liberal financial centre, they said.
"No one questions the effectiveness or necessity of the move but, if maintained over extended periods, it would hurt our image as an open, liberalised market," said a Thai bank dealer.
"In any game, players are expected to play by a set of pre-arranged rules. You just don't change it mid-way."

Since mid-May, the central bank has asked commercial banks to help curb baht speculation by quoting punitive baht/dollar swap rates to foreign hedge fund managers. Banks are allowed to continue quoting normal forward swap rates for trade and investment activities.

Some analysts said the two-tier baht system could possibly help bring down current high domestic interest rates by keeping baht supply from foreign speculators and so leaving the local market with plenty of liquidity.

The central bank's move, after the latest round of speculative attacks on the currency took place in early May, calmed money and foreign exchange markets but cut off baht funds needed by offshore speculators to push down the currency.

Currency dealers said in the first few days after the central bank introduced the measure, speculators betting with short forward baht positions faced prohibitive costs of over 1,000 percent a year to cover their baht/dollar contracts.

Dealers said some major speculators, hit by costly local currency funds and a stronger baht after joint Thai and Singapore central bank intervention, were rumoured to be facing hundreds of millions of dollars in losses two weeks ago.
On Wednesday, Thai banks quoted the one-month forward baht/dollar swap premium at 11/16 satang/dollar for domestic clients against 37/40 satang for foreign counterparts.
Dealers said, however, that the high foreign quotation hardly moved with almost no trading activity.

Thai central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Monday his bank would closely monitor the effect of the two-tier exchange rate system to ensure that it did not hurt normal business and investment. He did not say when it would be lifted.

Rerngchai's assistant Siri Ganjarerndee said on Tuesday the central bank would review the system from time to time depending on market confidence in the economy. He described the measure as over 90 percent effective in stopping baht speculation.
"The measure has reduced the number of daily baht/dollar transactions that we handle by at least 70 percent," a dealer at Bank of Ayudhya Plc said.
Most dealers said they saw no sign of the two-tier baht rate system becoming a barrier for non-speculative business although it may have slightly complicated some exchange deals.

"We have been told not to sell baht to foreign banks seeking funds for their own accounts but we still can offer baht quotes to foreign non-bank clients with real business background and to foreigners making portfolio investment in Thai stocks," a dealer at Hongkong and Shanghai Bank said.

Dealers said although the central bank had made an informal request for banks not to give speculators easy access to short-term baht, no commercial bank would provoke its ire by selling baht to speculators.
"Central bank auditors can check our transaction records. Speculative deals can be easily spotted," a dealer said.

Kanchit Assavasamrarn of Vickers Ballas and Co, echoing most analysts, said the central bank may feel more confident about relaxing its measure if the economy showed more convincing signs of recovery.
"We may not have to wait for the economy to fully recover as that may take a while. I think the central bank would feel more relaxed if sentiment on the baht looks more stable," he said.
